title: Introduce versioned metadata locks + sampled release-teaser generator
text:
Introduce versioned metadata locks + sampled release-teaser generator

description:
Summary: Adds a versioned metadata locking layer to the model registry to prevent conflicting profile edits and to provide auditable, transactional updates. Also introduces a sampled release-teaser generator that produces concise, telemetry-driven release snippets for changelogs and release notes drafts. Motivation: We observed occasional metadata stomping (parallel reviewer edits and automation hooks) and noisy/duplicative release notes authored manually. This PR reduces risk of merge conflicts, provides an explicit upgrade path for existing profiles, and automates concise release teasers so release engineers have a reliable starting point. Changes: 1) metadata-lock service: - New service layer (metadata/locks) that manages versioned locks using optimistic compare-and-swap backed by an advisory-lock fallback (Postgres advisory lock) for rare conflict windows. - Locks are coarse-grained at the profile ID + namespace level with an optional subkey (e.g., performance.profile) for targeted edits. - Each lock write increments a profile metadata version (profile_metadata_version), stored in registry_profiles.metadata_version (bigint). - API changes: PATCH /profiles/:id accepts if-match header (version token) and returns 412 on conflict with current metadata_version. 2) migration: - DB migration adds metadata_version column with default 1 and migrates existing ETags to initial versions for active profiles. - Migration is safe: reads are allowed during backfill; writes that race are rejected until backfill completes. 3) sampled release-teaser generator: - New module (releasenotes/teaser) that samples recent telemetry (latency, throughput delta, acceptance rate, rollout fraction) and generates 1-2 sentence teaser candidates ranked by impact. - Teasers are short, neutral language, and include an impact tag (e.g., perf, reliability, compatibility). - CLI integration: `rgm release-tease --profile <id> --window 7d` outputs top 3 candidate teasers and confidence scores. 4) UX/console: - Console shows an inline warning when you open a profile edit if you are editing a stale version, with a CTA to refresh or force-capture an updated baseline. - Release notes composer can import suggested teasers into the draft. 5) infra and tests: - Introduced advisory lock util and an in-memory fallthrough for unit tests. - Added unit tests for optimism conflict path and e2e test that simulates concurrent patchers. - Added benchmark harness for lock acquisition latency under 1000 concurrent simulated clients. Rationale and tradeoffs: - Optimistic-first reduces common-path latency for single-editor flows (majority of updates). Advisory locks prevent livelock during heavy automation-driven churn; we accept the small probability of a blocking fallback. - Changelog automation produces concise teasers only; full release notes still authored by humans. Checklist: - [x] DB migration script (non-blocking backfill) - [x] API contract updates with 412 behavior - [x] Unit tests for optimistic and fallback paths - [x] e2e concurrency test - [x] Console previews and CTA - [x] CLI integration for release-teaser drafts - [x] Benchmark harness for locks - [x] Docs: registry metadata locking, migration guidance, teaser rationale Rollout plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable metadata locks for 10% of orgs (feature flag) and generate teasers in dry-run mode. Observe conflict rates, lock latencies, and teaser adoption metrics. Phase 2: enable writes for all orgs and promote teasers to optional import in release composer. Phase 3: default-on for new orgs and opt-in for older orgs after migration window. Backwards compatibility: APIs will return 412 for stale writes; clients using older SDKs will receive explicit errors. We included SDK compatibility helpers and added a swift-fail guidance doc in redwood-sdk-* repos. Migration window and fallbacks are documented in upgrades/MIGRATION.md.

review_comments:
Diego Morales (2025-07-22): This looks good overall. Two concerns: how do we handle very large backfills and the window where clients might get repeated 412s? Suggest a backoff in SDK and a visible 'backfill in progress' flag in the console.
Maya Chen (2025-07-22): Reply: Agreed. Added backoff guidance to SDK compat helpers and we emit a backfill-in-progress flag via /registry/status which the console now surfaces.
Arjun Patel (2025-07-23): Could the sampled teaser generator leak PII through telemetry sampling? Please ensure we redact any identifiers before passing text to the teaser templates.
Maya Chen (2025-07-23): Reply: Teaser pipeline now runs a strict sanitizer that strips identifiers and normalizes numeric tokens. Added a unit test for sanitization.
Lena Ortiz (2025-07-24): Approve with one nit: the console CTA copy feels long. Suggest 'Refresh to get the latest metadata' instead of the current copy.
Maya Chen (2025-07-24): Reply: Updated CTA per feedback and adjusted translation keys.

release_notes:
- Introduced versioned metadata locking to prevent conflicting edits and provide explicit 412s for stale writes. SDK compatibility helpers added to simplify client-side retries and backoff.
- Added a sampled release-teaser generator that suggests concise, telemetry-weighted changelog snippets for release authors (CLI + Console integration).
- Safe DB migration for profile metadata versions with backfill guidance in docs.
Notes for operators: enable feature flag 'metadata-locks' to canary; review migration doc before full rollout.
